hardware.tested_state: existing flashed firmware image exercised by the review-scenario smoke tool

procedure: Ran NostrSeal/esp32 make ci after adding scripts/smoke_review_scenarios.py and the idf-smoke-review-scenarios target.
Exported ESP-IDF v5.5.4 from /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh in the same shell invocation used for the smoke.
Verified idf.py and esptool.py paths and confirmed idf.py --version reported ESP-IDF v5.5.4.
Ran make IDF_PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodem1101 idf-smoke-review-scenarios without reflashing, because the change added a smoke script and Makefile target only.
The smoke sent the basic, tagged, long-content, scroll-window, Unicode fallback, and request-error review scenarios over USB serial.
expected_result: The existing flashed firmware preserves the disabled-signing USB protocol contract for all review scenarios: valid sign_event review requests return signing_disabled, and the request-error scenario returns deterministic unsupported_request for the invalid request.
observed_result: ESP-IDF v5.5.4 environment resolved idf.py under /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/tools/idf.py and esptool.py under /Users/vincenzo/.espressif/python_env/idf5.5_py3.9_env/bin/esptool.py. The review-scenario smoke passed: 6 scenarios, 7 verified serial exchanges, 6 response frames, and 1 expected rejection frame. Valid sign_event review scenarios still returned signing_disabled, and the invalid request returned unsupported_request.
limitations: Protocol smoke only; it does not visually verify that every review scenario was rendered correctly on the physical display.
The run did not test physical button approve/reject input, key provisioning, storage, secure boot, flash encryption, debug lock, companion signed-output verification, or real signing acceptance.
The board was not reflashed for this report because the ESP32 firmware code did not change; the smoke exercised the existing flashed firmware image.
sign_event is expected to remain signing_disabled until trusted display review, physical approval, provisioning, storage, signed-output verification, and firmware hardening gates are complete.
